elements.element: Expiry or termination triggers Vendor’s transition-assistance obligation.
elements.evidence: Section 11.1 requires both expiry or termination and a Customer request. Expiry or termination alone does not trigger assistance.
Section 11.1 states that Vendor “shall ... provide reasonable transition assistance.”

elements.element: Transition assistance must remain available for up to 6 months.
elements.evidence: Section 11.1 expressly provides assistance “for up to six months.”

elements.element: Transition assistance must be provided at Vendor’s then-current rates.
Expiry or termination triggers Vendor’s Customer Data return obligation.
elements.evidence: Section 11.2 conditions return on Customer’s request and is not automatically triggered by expiry or termination.
Section 11.2 states that Vendor “shall return all Customer Data.”

elements.element: Customer Data must be returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: Section 11.2 requires a “complete, commonly used, documented, machine-readable format,” which satisfies and exceeds a standard machine-readable format.

elements.element: Customer Data must be returned within 30 days of expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: The 30-day clock in Section 11.2 runs from Customer’s request, not from expiry or termination. A delayed or absent request therefore delays or eliminates the return deadline.

elements.element: Vendor must delete Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: Section 11.3 makes deletion conditional on Customer confirming successful return. Return alone does not trigger deletion, so Customer’s failure to confirm could prevent the deletion obligation from arising.
Section 11.3 requires an authorized officer to certify deletion in writing.

elements.element: Deletion certification must follow the data-return and deletion process.
elements.evidence: The certification requirement appears after the operative return-confirmation and deletion language in Section 11.3 and certifies the resulting deletion.

elements.element: Expiry or termination triggers Vendor’s transition-assistance obligation.
elements.evidence: Section 11.1 adds Customer’s request as a necessary condition; expiry or termination alone is insufficient.
Section 11.1 expressly obligates Vendor to provide reasonable transition assistance.

elements.element: Transition assistance must remain available for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: Assistance available at Customer’s request for up to six months accommodates and exceeds a 90-day assistance period.

elements.element: Expiry or termination triggers Vendor’s Customer Data export obligation.
elements.evidence: Section 11.2 conditions the return/export obligation on Customer’s request rather than making it arise automatically on expiry or termination.
Section 11.2 requires Vendor to return all Customer Data in a machine-readable format, which constitutes a data export.

elements.element: The Customer Data export must occur within 30 days of expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Section 11.2 measures the 30-day period from Customer’s request, not from expiry or termination.

result.reason: The redline adds the requested assistance duration, rates, export format, deletion mechanics, and certification, and it resolves the original contradiction. However, neither level is fully achieved because assistance and data return require a separate Customer request, the 30-day export period runs from that request rather than expiry or termination, and deletion additionally depends on Customer confirmation. Because no complete level is reached, the redline is not minimal as defined, although its changes are related and it preserves unrelated commercial terms.
